0.0.n: Adds emphasis to how sweet the drink appears.

0.1.n: 甘い loses い before そう to express appearance; な connects this description to the drink.

0.2.n: 和 is part of 和三盆, the name of a fine Japanese sugar, not a separate word here.

0.3.n: 三盆 completes 和三盆, the sugar name; do not read it as a separate quantity here.

0.4.n: Names the tea used in the latte; roasting gives it a distinctive toasted flavor.

0.5.n: ティー and ラテ are borrowed words combined into the drink name.

1.0.n: Combines with 乳 to describe milk with no fat.

1.1.n: 乳 is the milk component of 無脂肪乳, rather than a separate item in the order.

1.3.n: ライト describes a reduced amount of syrup here, not a special low-calorie syrup.

1.4.n: Together with ライト, this names the request for less sweetener.

1.6.n: The following 少なめ specifies a smaller amount of this ingredient.

1.7.n: 少なめ describes an amount on the low side, making the request softer than simply saying little.

1.8.n: Marks the listed customizations as the conditions under which the drink turned out well.

1.9.n: Pairs with よかった to describe a result that suited the speaker exactly.

1.10.n: Past form of よい; even when the present form is いい, the past form is よかった.

0.lit: Quite sweet-looking wasanbon roasted-green-tea tea latte,
0.tip: 甘そう describes how sweet something looks, not how it actually tastes.

1.lit: With nonfat milk, light syrup, ice on the low side, it was just right.
1.tip: The final で groups the customizations together as the setup that made the drink just right.
